title: When the Witness Falls
premise: Oscar Blackwood, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with a private gift for reading the gaps in official stories, is pulled into a murder investigation when a corpse surfaces wearing clothes stolen from his own closet — a message meant to silence him. The victim was the last person to see Vivian Marsh alive, the heiress whose death sealed her family's fortune and whom everyone insists is dead. As Oscar digs through the Blackwood-adjacent world of lawyers, drivers, and old money, he discovers Vivian staged her own disappearance to escape a family that kills for inheritance, and that someone inside her circle has been murdering witnesses ever since. In the end Oscar finds Vivian hiding in plain sight as a night dispatcher at a rival cab company, exposes her uncle's killing spree with a trap built from dispatch logs, and must choose between turning her over for faking her death or letting justice outside the law stand.
about_author: Gideon Sandoval spent eleven years working overnight shifts at a municipal transit authority before turning to crime fiction full-time. He writes his novels between midnight and dawn, claiming the city confesses more honestly after 2 a.m.

chapters.title: The Third Accident
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. On a slow night shift, Oscar reads a news brief about a dockworker's 'accidental' fall and recognizes the same pattern from two earlier deaths he quietly unraveled. He keeps a notebook of discrepancies no one asked him to keep. The beat establishes his obsessive, lonely competence and the itch that something bigger is coming.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Police wake him at dawn: a body pulled from the river wearing Oscar's own jacket, shirt, and shoes, stolen from his building's laundry room. Detective Ilsa Reyes treats him as suspect first, witness second. The emotional beat is violation and fear — someone knows his routines intimately enough to impersonate him.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Was Buried
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. The victim is identified as Daniel Voss, notary to the Marsh estate, officially listed five years ago as the sole witness to heiress Vivian Marsh's death certificate. Oscar realizes Voss was alive all along and hiding. Beat: vertigo — the case is older and colder than it looked.

chapters.title: Reyes Doesn't Believe in Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Oscar/Reyes. Reyes shares a sealed file: Vivian Marsh drowned, closed case, family pressure everywhere. Oscar shows her his notebook of three solved 'accidents'; she calls it luck but pockets a copy. Beat: wary alliance formed out of mutual use, neither trusting the other.

chapters.title: Old Money, Older Grudges
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Oscar works the Marsh orbit: Uncle Alistair Marsh, who controls the trust; the family lawyer; a disinherited cousin. Everyone performs grief like a rehearsed play. He notices Alistair's driver takes suspiciously convenient routes. Beat: the corrupting gravity of inherited wealth made visible.

chapters.title: Dispatch Logs Don't Lie
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Cross-referencing taxi records, Oscar finds Voss took regular late-night rides to a shuttered ferry terminal — a dead man commuting. Someone else rode those routes too, always paying cash. Beat: hunter's thrill, the first hard thread connecting Voss to a living accomplice.

chapters.title: A Threat in His Own Handwriting
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Oscar receives a note written in his own handwriting, quoting his private notebook verbatim — pages only Reyes has seen. Confrontation turns cold; either she leaked it or someone inside the precinct did. Beat: betrayal and paranoia; the alliance cracks.

chapters.title: The Ferry Terminal
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Night search of the terminal yields Voss's hidden locker: ledgers proving the Marsh trust was built on forged documents, and a photograph of Vivian alive, taken two years ago. Oscar is ambushed and barely escapes. Beat: proof in hand, price nearly paid.

chapters.title: What the Family Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Reyes. Reyes pulls the original drowning file and finds the responding officer was later hired by Alistair Marsh. She begins her own quiet audit, off the books. Beat: her arc pivots from gatekeeper of the law to doubter of it.

chapters.title: The Cousin Who Talked
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Disinherited cousin Lena Marsh tells Oscar Vivian feared her uncle would kill her before her twenty-fifth birthday, when the trust would have passed to her outright. Two days later Lena is found dead — another accident. Beat: guilt and fury; talking to Oscar now carries a body count.

chapters.title: Dead Man Driving
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Oscar identifies the cash-paying passenger on Voss's routes: a rival cab company's night dispatcher known only as 'Vee.' The voice on an old dispatch recording stops him cold — it's a woman's, calm and familiar. Beat: the hunt narrows to one impossible person.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Oscar and Reyes, reconciled by necessity, compare notes: three witnesses to the Marsh fraud are dead, all ruled accidental, all connected to Voss. The killer isn't hiding the truth — they're erasing its footnotes. Beat: dread of scale; the pattern completes itself.

chapters.title: The Man in the Closet
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Oscar finds evidence the clothes thief is someone with access to both his building and police channels — a former patrol officer now on Alistair's payroll. Watching his own apartment, he sees the man return to plant more 'evidence.' Beat: reversal; Oscar becomes the trap-setter instead of the prey.

chapters.title: Twenty-Five Candles
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Flashback chapter via Voss's ledgers and Lena's letters reconstructing Vivian's story: abused heir, staged drowning with Voss's help, then Voss's greed turning to blackmail. Beat: sympathy deepens — Vivian fled corruption, not justice, but left witnesses to die.

chapters.title: Midnight Frequency
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Using dispatch codes, Oscar sends a message across every cab channel in the city addressed to 'Vee': I know you're alive, and so does whoever killed Voss. At 3 a.m., a reply comes from a payphone number. Beat: breathless contact; the ghost answers.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Other End
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Oscar/Vivian. Meeting in a laundromat — echoing the stolen clothes — Vivian admits everything but swears she didn't kill Voss. She reveals Alistair's fixer has been hunting her for years and using her trail to find loose ends. Beat: fragile trust; two fugitives from different kinds of law.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Reyes. Reyes traces the ex-cop fixer's payments and finds the fourth name on his list: Oscar himself, scheduled next. She must decide whether to report through channels that are compromised or go around them. Beat: her choice — justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Oscar lets the fixer believe Vivian will retrieve the ledgers from the ferry terminal, feeding the plan through the precinct leak. Reyes positions herself off-book; Vivian insists on being present. Beat: coiled tension, everyone gambling on everyone else's desperation.

chapters.title: Accidents, Reversed
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The trap springs at the terminal: the fixer confesses to three staged deaths while trying to stage a fourth, recorded by Reyes and witnessed by Vivian from the shadows. Alistair arrives expecting cleanup and walks into the light instead. Beat: climax — violence contained, truth finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: POV: Reyes. Alistair's lawyers move instantly; the forged-trust evidence is admissible, but Vivian's faked death is a crime. Reyes must choose what to file and what to lose. Beat: moral weight — the law vindicated and indicted in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Witness Falls
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Vivian agrees to testify in exchange for leniency, ending her five-year death. On the courthouse steps she thanks Oscar for finding the one thing the family couldn't buy: a stranger who kept asking questions. Beat: bittersweet resolution; the witness falls back into the world, alive.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: POV: Oscar. Weeks later, Oscar returns to the dispatch desk, notebook thinner, phone quieter. Reyes sends him a single line: the fourth accident never happened. He opens a fresh page anyway. Beat: quiet closure and open horizon — the watcher returns to watching.
